explanation: Ventris trained at London's Architectural Association and had chased the puzzle since hearing Arthur Evans lecture when he was 14. Linear B turned out to record Mycenaean Greek.

claims.text: Michael Ventris, who deciphered Linear B in 1952, was an architect by profession.
Ventris was not a professional codebreaker, museum curator or classics professor.
Ventris trained at the Architectural Association School of Architecture in London.
At 14, Ventris heard Arthur Evans lecture on Minoan Crete and became fascinated by its scripts.
